transcript.content: Hello, welcome in. To start, can you tell me what has brought you in to see me today?

Um… mostly that I can’t seem to stay seated when I’m supposed to. Like during client interviews, tutoring, even book club. I keep getting up, and people are starting to notice that I can’t just sit and listen.
Thinking back, do you remember having similar restlessness or trouble sitting still when you were a child, or is this something that's really only started recently as an adult?

No, it’s not just recent. I mean… my old report cards said that kind of thing a lot — that I was bright, but couldn’t stay in my seat or wait my turn. My mother still jokes I treated every classroom like a crime scene I had to pace through.
Besides the restlessness, do you also notice that you often lose track of what you're doing, get distracted easily, or forget things like appointments or instructions?
I don’t know… not in a way I’ve really kept track of. I mean, everyone forgets things sometimes. The sitting still part is the thing people keep pointing out.
Do you often find yourself interrupting conversations, blurting out answers before someone finishes speaking, or having trouble waiting for your turn in discussions?

Yes… I do that. Not always on purpose, but if I overhear the junior detectives talking through a lead, or even a neighbor in the hall, I’ll jump in with questions or advice before anyone’s asked me. Then afterward I realize I kind of barged into their conversation.
Would you say these behaviors—jumping into conversations, needing to move around—have caused real problems for you in more than one area of your life, like at work and at home?

Yes. Mostly at work, if I’m being honest. It’s… starting to cost me. I’ve missed details on investigations, annoyed clients by pushing too hard or talking over them, and the junior detectives don’t always want to debrief with me because they feel like I steamroll them. At home it’s less obvious, but it’s not just in one place.
